source_title: lululemon athletica inc. Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year Fiscal 2014 Results
publisher_issuer: lululemon athletica inc. (investor-relations results release; corresponds to Form 8-K exhibit, EDGAR CIK 0001397187)
company_context: In March 2013 Lululemon recalled certain black Luon yoga pants for being too sheer, triggering a quality-and-trust crisis, inventory and margin damage, and leadership turnover. This record focuses on the RECOVERY in fiscal 2014 (year ended February 1, 2015), when the brand returned to revenue and comparable-sales growth after the recall.
business_type: Premium technical athletic apparel (vertical retail and direct-to-consumer)
geography: North America-led, with international growth (headquartered Canada)
time_period: FY2014 (year ended February 1, 2015), compared with FY2013
macro_context: Growing athleisure/athletic-apparel demand; heightened competition (Athleta, Under Armour, Nike); brand still rebuilding consumer trust and product-quality reputation after the 2013 recall.
evidence_summary: After the 2013 sheer-pants recall shock, Lululemon recovered demand and growth in fiscal 2014. Full-year net revenue increased 13% to $1.8 billion from $1.6 billion in fiscal 2013, with total comparable sales up 3% on a constant-dollar basis. The fourth quarter (ended February 1, 2015) showed acceleration: net revenue up 16% to $602.5 million from $521 million in Q4 fiscal 2013, with total comparable sales (stores plus direct-to-consumer) up 8% on a constant-dollar basis, indicating restored customer trust and momentum.
owner_decision_context: Following the recall and leadership changes, management chose to rebuild product-quality controls and brand trust and to keep investing in stores and direct-to-consumer rather than retrench, betting that restored quality perception would re-accelerate demand.
action_taken: Strengthened quality and sourcing oversight, refreshed leadership, and continued store and e-commerce growth, allowing comparable sales and revenue to re-accelerate through fiscal 2014.
outcome_evidence: FY2014 net revenue up 13% to $1.8B with comp sales up 3%, accelerating to Q4 revenue up 16% to $602.5M and comp sales up 8%, confirms recovery from the 2013 quality/trust shock.

The pattern of a sharp prior-year shock followed by within-year recovery is best classified as temporary shock with recovery
why_useful_for_opsiq: A quality/trust shock followed by a documented demand recovery, useful for testing whether the engine treats a recall as a recoverable temporary shock (with the recovery evidenced by reaccelerating comps) rather than permanent impairment. Focus is deliberately on the recovery, not the recall.
